id: ROOT
name: GitHub Collaboration Platform Core Requirements
type: FOLDER
dependencies: []
description: This product is a simplified GitHub collaboration platform. Unless an
  atomic requirement explicitly allows more than one role, every quoted user-interface
  name is the exact English accessible name of the control; the role, scope, and observable-state
  rules stated by each atomic requirement are authoritative. Values described as existing
  accounts, organizations, teams, repositories, branches, files, commits, issues,
  milestones, pull requests, reviews, and permission relationships are predefined
  seed data. The application must provision those records before the corresponding
  scenario and supply each account through an isolated browser session; they are not
  extra features that a participant must expose through a private API. Generated
  names may contain a unique suffix, but their role, ownership, visibility, and relationships
  are exactly those stated in the atomic requirement. Every atomic requirement remains
  enabled even when seed configuration is incomplete. Organization Owner, repository Admin, Read,
  Triage, Write, Maintain, and Admin permissions follow the operation-specific rules
  in the requirements below; these roles are not an automatic cumulative ladder. Real-time
  collaboration, Actions, Packages, Wiki, project boards, notification delivery, and
  external Git remote protocols are outside the scope of this product.
children:
- id: REQ-1
  name: Identity and Access
  type: FOLDER
  dependencies: []
  description: This module defines the “account” and “session” required to access
    the system. An account is a persistent individual identity storing a username,
    verified email, and credential status; a session is a record created after successful
    account sign-in that represents only the current browser login state. Visitors
    enter the account-access page from “Sign up”, “Sign in”, or “Forgot password”
    on the home page; signed-in users enter security settings or sign out from the
    account menu. The account menu is the control in the upper-right corner of the
    page that displays the current signed-in account, organization list, and sign-out
    entry. No page, error message, or recovery flow may display a full password. After
    successful sign-in, the account menu displays the current user, and subsequent
    organization, repository, issue, and pull-request pages use this session to determine
    visibility and operation permissions; sign-out, password changes, and recovery
    must immediately change the session state visible to subsequent requests.
  children:
  - id: REQ-1-1
    name: Account Registration and Recovery
    type: FOLDER
    dependencies: []
    description: The account-access page is the shared page used by unauthenticated
      users to register, sign in, and recover a password, with the frontend showing
      the appropriate form and submit button for each operation. The local product
      does not implement an email-verification page, email delivery, or an external
      verification-code service — successful registration directly stores a sign-in-capable
      account and marks its email as verified; successful sign-in only stores a new
      session and does not create a duplicate account; after submitting an email for
      password recovery, the page directly displays the fixed verification code `123456`
      and the password-reset form, and only the correct code together with a compliant
      new password updates the password of the same account. Registration, sign-in,
      and recovery pages must use visible labels to identify fields and submit actions;
      after failure, non-sensitive input is retained, while password and password-confirmation
      fields must not redisplay submitted values.
    children:
    - id: REQ-1-1-1
      name: Register a New GitHub Account
      type: ATOMIC
      dependencies: []
      description: |-
        The registration page is the form opened by the unique link named “Create an account” from the sign-in page. The form contains exactly one textbox labeled “Username”, one textbox labeled “Email”, one password input labeled “Password”, one password input labeled “Confirm password”, one initially unchecked checkbox named “Agree to the terms”, and one enabled button named “Create account”. The username and email identify the account, while passwords must not be echoed on the page. This product directly marks the email of a successfully registered account as verified and does not provide a subsequent email-verification page. The visitor enters a unique username, email, password, and matching confirmation, checks “Agree to the terms”, and activates “Create account”. The username must consist of 1 to 39 lowercase ASCII letters, digits, or single hyphens (`-`) and must not begin or end with a hyphen; after trimming leading and trailing whitespace, the email must contain exactly one `@`, be no longer than 254 characters, and have at least one dot and non-empty domain labels after the `@`; the password must contain 12 to 128 characters, include at least one uppercase letter, one lowercase letter, one digit, and one non-alphanumeric special character, and contain no whitespace characters. The system stores a sign-in-capable account together with its verified-email status and enters the sign-in page; if the username or email conflicts, any field is missing, the email format is invalid, the terms are not accepted, the password is noncompliant, or the confirmation does not match, the system retains the username and email input, displays an itemized message beside the corresponding field, and does not create an account. The corresponding visible field message contains “Username already exists”, “Username format is invalid”, “Email format is invalid”, “Password requirements are not satisfied”, or “Agree to terms is required”, as applicable. Visitors can use this capability on the account-access page. The system validates input rules, displays field errors, and prevents duplicate accounts; on success, it directly creates an available account. Submitting several invalid fields together must show the username, email, password, and missing-terms messages together, rather than revealing only one error per submission; the submit button remains actionable so these messages can be read. For example, a username beginning with a hyphen, email “not-an-email”, password “short”, confirmation “different”, and unchecked terms produce these field errors and preserve the attempted username. A duplicate username paired with a different unused email displays “Username already exists” and retains both attempted values. A successful registration accepts a unique username, its email, and password; the sign-in form is immediately available, accepts that email, and the resulting signed-in username remains visible after reload.

        Screenshot reference:
        ![image](reference/github-sign-up.png)
      scenarios:
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-1: Register a New GitHub Account - Scenario 1'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts at the application home page in a fresh unauthenticated
            browser session and opens the account-access page. The visitor clicks the visible
            link “Sign in” and then the visible link “Create an account”. The registration page
            displays visibly labeled Username, Email, Password, and Confirm password fields,
            a checkbox named “Agree to the terms”, and a button named “Create account”. The
            username `nora-demo` and email `nora.demo@example.test` are not registered.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor enters `nora-demo` in Username, `nora.demo@example.test` in
            Email, `Valid-password-123!` in Password and Confirm password, checks “Agree to
            the terms”, and clicks “Create account”.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The system opens the sign-in page and visibly displays the labeled “Username
            or email” and “Password” fields and the “Sign in” button. The visitor enters
            `nora.demo@example.test` in “Username or email”, enters `Valid-password-123!` in
            “Password”, and clicks “Sign in”. The workspace visibly displays the username
            `nora-demo`.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'After the visitor reloads the page, the workspace still visibly displays
            the username `nora-demo`.'
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-1: Register a New GitHub Account - Scenario 2'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts at the application home page in a fresh unauthenticated
            browser session and opens the account-access page. The visitor opens the
            registration page through the visible “Sign in” and “Create an account” links.
            The registration page displays visibly labeled Username, Email, Password, and
            Confirm password fields, a checkbox named “Agree to the terms”, and a button
            named “Create account”.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor enters the invalid username `-invalid-demo` in Username,
            `invalid.username@example.test` in Email, `Valid-password-123!` in Password
            and Confirm password, checks “Agree to the terms”, and clicks “Create account”.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The registration page remains open and displays “Username format is
            invalid”. The Username field retains the value `-invalid-demo`; no account is
            created.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The Email, Password, Confirm password, and terms controls remain available
            for correction, and the rejected submission does not redirect to the sign-in page.'
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-1: Register a New GitHub Account - Scenario 3'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts at the application home page in a fresh unauthenticated
            browser session and opens the account-access page. The visitor opens the
            registration page through the visible “Sign in” and “Create an account” links.
            The registration page displays visibly labeled Username, Email, Password, and
            Confirm password fields, a checkbox named “Agree to the terms”, and a button
            named “Create account”. The username `invalid-email-demo` is unused.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor enters `invalid-email-demo` in Username, the invalid email
            `not-an-email` in Email, `Valid-password-123!` in Password and Confirm password,
            checks “Agree to the terms”, and clicks “Create account”.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The registration page remains open and displays “Email format is invalid”.
            The Email field retains the value `not-an-email`; no account is created.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The valid Username, Password, Confirm password, and terms controls remain
            available for correction, and the rejected submission does not redirect to the
            sign-in page.'
    - id: REQ-1-1-2
      name: Sign In with an Existing Account
      type: ATOMIC
      dependencies:
      - REQ-1-1-1
      description: |-
        This feature builds on the persisted objects. The sign-in page is the form on the account-access page containing “Username or email”, “Password”, and “Sign in”. A “session” is the current-browser login record saved after successful account authentication, represented in the frontend by the upper-right account menu and access to protected pages. The visitor enters a username or email and a password and submits the form. The system looks up the account and validates its credentials and availability status; if authentication fails due to an unknown username/email, incorrect password, or unavailable account, the system displays exactly the same generic failure message “Invalid credentials”, does not disclose whether the account exists or which credential was wrong, and does not create a session. After successful authentication, the system stores a session with a unique session identifier, account identifier, and active status, then redirects to the workspace accessible to that user; the session remains valid after refreshing or reopening the workspace, and subsequent protected organization, repository, and work-item requests must use this session to determine the current user.

        Screenshot reference:
        ![image](reference/github-sign-in.png)
      scenarios:
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-2: Sign In with an Existing Account - Scenario 1'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts in a fresh unauthenticated browser session. The
            system has pre-provisioned a verified and available account with username
            `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`, and password
            `Valid-password-123!`.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor opens the application home page, verifies that exactly one
            visible link named “Sign in” is available, and clicks it. On the sign-in page,
            the visitor enters `alice-dev` in the visibly labeled “Username or email” field,
            enters `Valid-password-123!` in the visibly labeled “Password” field, and clicks
            the button named “Sign in”.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The system enters the workspace and visibly displays the exact username
            `alice-dev`.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'After the visitor reloads the page, the exact username `alice-dev`
            remains visible.'
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-2: Sign In with an Existing Account - Scenario 2'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts in a fresh unauthenticated browser session. The
            system has pre-provisioned a verified and available account with username
            `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`, and password
            `Valid-password-123!`.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor opens the application home page, clicks the visible link
            named “Sign in”, enters `alice.dev@example.test` in the visibly labeled
            “Username or email” field, enters the incorrect password
            `Valid-password-123!-incorrect` in the visibly labeled “Password” field, and
            clicks the button named “Sign in”.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The sign-in page visibly displays the generic message “Invalid
            credentials”.'
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-2: Sign In with an Existing Account - Scenario 3'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts in a fresh unauthenticated browser session. The
            system has pre-provisioned a verified and available account with username
            `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`, and password
            `Valid-password-123!`.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor opens the application home page, clicks the visible link
            named “Sign in”, enters `alice.dev@example.test` in the visibly labeled
            “Username or email” field, enters `Valid-password-123!` in the visibly labeled
            “Password” field, and clicks the button named “Sign in”.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The system enters the workspace and visibly displays the username
            `alice-dev`.'
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-2: Sign In with an Existing Account - Scenario 4'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts in a fresh unauthenticated browser session. The
            system has pre-provisioned a verified and available account with username
            `alice-dev`, email `alice.dev@example.test`, and password
            `Valid-password-123!`.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor opens the application home page, clicks the visible link
            named “Sign in”, enters the unknown address `unknown@example.test` in the
            visibly labeled “Username or email” field, enters `Valid-password-123!` in
            “Password”, and clicks “Sign in”. The visitor then reopens the application home
            page, clicks “Sign in” again, enters `alice-dev` in “Username or email”, enters
            the incorrect password `Valid-password-123!-wrong` in “Password”, and clicks
            “Sign in” again.'
        - keyword: THEN
          content: 'The first sign-in attempt displays the generic message “Invalid
            credentials”, and the second sign-in attempt displays the same generic message.'
    - id: REQ-1-1-3
      name: Recover Account Access Through a Verified Email
      type: ATOMIC
      dependencies:
      - REQ-1-1-1
      description: The sign-in page exposes a visible “Forgot password” link. The recovery
        step displays visibly labeled Email, Verification code, New password, and Confirm
        password fields and a “Send reset link” or “Reset password” button. A registered
        verified email and an unknown email both reach the same recovery step and display
        the fixed verification code `123456` without requiring email delivery. A wrong code
        leaves the original password usable and displays “Verification code is invalid”. A
        correct code with matching compliant passwords updates the account and displays
        “Password updated”.
      scenarios:
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-3: Recover Account Access Through a Verified Email - Scenario
          1'
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: 'The visitor starts in a fresh unauthenticated browser session. Test setup
            pre-provisions the verified account `recovery-visibility` with email
            `recovery-visibility@example.test` and password `Valid-password-123!`; the
            address `unknown@example.test` does not belong to an account.'
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: 'The visitor opens “Sign in”, clicks “Forgot password”, submits
            `recovery-visibility@example.test`, and then repeats the reset-step flow for
            `unknown@example.test`.'

          content: 'Both reset-step pages display the fixed text `123456`, the visibly labeled
            “Verification code” field, and the visibly labeled “New password” field.'
      - name: 'REQ-1-1-3: Recover Account Access Through a Verified Email - Scenario

id: ROOT
name: Core Requirements for an Online Spreadsheet Data Workspace
type: FOLDER
dependencies: []
description: 'A streamlined online spreadsheet application with an interface modeled
  after Google Sheets, covering workbook and worksheet management, spreadsheet data
  editing, formula calculation, sorting and filtering, data validation, and basic
  pivot analysis. Sharing and collaboration, version-history restoration, advanced
  visual styling, charts, macros, real-time collaborative cursors, and integrations
  with external office suites are outside the core scope.

  '
children:
- id: REQ-1
  name: Workbook Access and Lifecycle
  type: FOLDER
  dependencies: []
  description: 'Supports viewing, opening, creating, renaming, importing, and exporting
    workbooks within the application. The home page is the entry point for workbooks;
    successful open, create, and import operations all enter the same editor page,
    and subsequent operations may modify only the currently opened workbook. After
    a workbook is opened, created, or imported, the editor state shown in the browser
    must be a stable workbook state: visiting or refreshing that
    exact workbook state must open the same workbook rather than another workbook or a temporary
    blank page, and successful workbook modifications must remain available through
    that visible workbook state. After returning to the home page or reopening, the workbook name, last-updated
    time, worksheet order, and last active worksheet remain consistent. Worksheet
    tabs on the same editor page use the ARIA tab role, with the active tab indicated
    by aria-selected="true"; the active worksheet grid uses the ARIA grid role, has
    the accessible name "Worksheet grid", and exposes aria-multiselectable="true".
    Grid cells use the ARIA gridcell role with their cell coordinates as accessible
    names (for example, A1); the current cell and every cell within the currently
    selected rectangular region expose aria-selected="true", while cells outside the
    region expose aria-selected="false".

    '
  children:
  - id: REQ-1-1
    name: Workbook Navigation
    type: FOLDER
    dependencies: []
    description: |
      Supports viewing and opening available workbooks from the home page. After a workbook is successfully created, renamed, or imported from CSV, returning to or refreshing the home page must show the updated record in the list.

      Page reference:
      ![image](reference/workbook-home.png)
    children:
    - id: REQ-1-1-1
      name: View and Open a Workbook
      type: ATOMIC
      dependencies: []
      description: |
        Users view available workbooks on the workbook home page. Each record displays "Last updated: <last updated value>" and provides a link whose accessible name is the workbook name. After the user clicks the link, the editor displays the same "Last updated: <last updated value>", the corresponding workbook name, worksheet tabs and order, current active worksheet, row and column structure, grid values, formula bar content, filter views, validation entry points, and pivot table results; data from another workbook must not appear in the current grid. The current editor page entry in the browser must be directly accessible and continue to identify the same workbook after refresh; visiting that exact workbook state in the same or a later browser session must restore the workbook’s most recent successful state without requiring navigation through the home page. The entry format is implementation-defined.

        Page reference:
        ![image](reference/workbook-home.png)
      scenarios:
      - name: REQ-1-1-1 - View and Open a Workbook - Scenario 1
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: The visitor starts on the home page with no workbook selected.
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: The user creates a blank workbook, renames it with a runtime-unique name,
            enters a runtime-unique value in A1, returns home, and opens that workbook link.
        - keyword: THEN
          content: The editor shows the same workbook name, last-updated text, active Sheet1,
            and the value in A1; after refresh and in a new browser session, the workbook
            and A1 value remain visible.
      - name: REQ-1-1-1 - View and Open a Workbook - Scenario 2
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: Two blank workbooks have been created, each with a different runtime-unique
            name and a different value in A1.
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: The user returns home, opens the first workbook, and refreshes the editor.
        - keyword: THEN
          content: A1 contains the first workbook's value and the second workbook's value
            is absent both before and after refresh.
  - id: REQ-1-2
    name: Workbook Creation and Naming
    type: FOLDER
    dependencies: []
    description: 'Supports creating a blank workbook and changing the workbook name;
      both operations are initiated from visible workbook state points on the home page or
      editor page. After success, the workbook record on the home page and the editor
      title are updated consistently and remain so after refresh or reopening.

      '
    children:
    - id: REQ-1-2-1
      name: Create a Blank Workbook
      type: ATOMIC
      dependencies: []
      description: |
        Users create a blank workbook from the workbook home page. The home page provides a button with the accessible name "New blank workbook"; clicking it opens the creation page, whose submit button is named "Create". After creation succeeds, the editor opens and shows only a blank worksheet named Sheet1, with Sheet1 active and A1 selected; refreshing or returning to the home page and reopening produces the same state. If creation fails, an error is displayed, the user remains in a retryable state, and no incomplete workbook record may appear on the home page.

        Page reference:
        ![image](reference/create-workbook.png)
      scenarios:
      - name: REQ-1-2-1 - Create a Blank Workbook - Scenario 1
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: The visitor is on the workbook home page.
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: The user clicks New blank workbook, submits the creation page with Create,
            and refreshes the editor.
        - keyword: THEN
          content: The editor contains only blank Sheet1, Sheet1 is active, A1 is selected
            and empty, and those states remain after refresh.
    - id: REQ-1-2-2
      name: Rename a Workbook
      type: ATOMIC
      dependencies:
      - REQ-1-1-1
      description: 'Users can change the workbook name on the workbook editor page.
        Next to the editor title is a button with the accessible name "Rename workbook";
        clicking it displays a text box labeled "Workbook name", prefilled with the
        last saved name, and a "Save" button. After leading and trailing spaces are
        trimmed, the name must not be empty; an empty name must be rejected with "Workbook
        name cannot be empty". After a successful save, both the editor title and
        the home-page link display the new name; if saving fails, an error is shown
        and the original name remains displayed. Reopening the workbook shows the
        most recently saved name.

        '
      scenarios:
      - name: REQ-1-2-2 - Rename a Workbook - Scenario 1
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: A newly created workbook contains Existing data in A1.
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: The user opens Rename workbook, enters a runtime-unique name surrounded
            by spaces, submits with Enter, returns home, reopens the renamed link, and opens
            the rename dialog again.
        - keyword: THEN
          content: Leading and trailing spaces are removed; the editor and home link show
            the new name, A1 still contains Existing data, and the reopened dialog is prefilled
            with the trimmed name.
      - name: REQ-1-2-2 - Rename a Workbook - Scenario 2
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: A newly created workbook is open with a non-empty original name.
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: The user enters only spaces in the Workbook name field and submits Save,
            then refreshes and reopens the rename dialog.
        - keyword: THEN
          content: The message Workbook name cannot be empty is visible; the original name
            remains in the editor and the reopened field.
  - id: REQ-1-3
    name: CSV Data Exchange
    type: FOLDER
    dependencies: []
    description: 'Supports importing external CSV data completely as a workbook and
      exporting the current active worksheet as CSV. After a successful import, the
      Sheet1 editor page opens and continues to show the complete imported result
      after refresh or reopening; export reads only the current active worksheet and
      must not change workbook content or the current interface state.

      '
    children:
    - id: REQ-1-3-1
      name: Import CSV to Create a Workbook
      type: ATOMIC
      dependencies: []
      description: 'Users start an import by clicking the "Import CSV" button on the
        workbook home page. A dialog named "Import CSV" provides a file control labeled
        "CSV file" and a "Confirm import" button. The system parses data in the original
        row and column order, preserves empty fields, supports UTF-8 Chinese text,
        English text, and numeric text, and correctly handles commas enclosed in double
        quotes, escaped pairs of double quotes, and line breaks within fields; a field
        that begins with a double quote but has no closing double quote is invalid
        CSV and must be rejected with "Invalid CSV file format. Import failed." After
        a successful import, a new workbook is created whose name is the file name
        with its final .csv extension removed, and Sheet1 opens with the complete
        CSV rows, columns, and original text; the first row remains ordinary data.
        After refresh or reopening, grid content and row/column order remain unchanged.
        If parsing or import fails, no workbook link with that name may appear on
        the home page, and no partial import result may be displayed or retained.

        '
      scenarios:
      - name: REQ-1-3-1 - Import CSV to Create a Workbook - Scenario 1
        steps:
        - keyword: GIVEN
          content: The visitor is on the workbook home page and has a CSV containing quoted
            commas, a quoted newline and quote escapes, numeric text including 007, and
            blank fields.
        - keyword: WHEN
          content: The user opens Import CSV, uploads the CSV, and confirms the import.
        - keyword: THEN
          content: A workbook named from the uploaded file is opened on Sheet1; headers,
            quoted text, 42, 3, 007, and blank D2/D3/D4 cells appear in the asserted coordinates
            and remain after refresh.

    59	def copy_template_contents(template_dir: Path, output_dir: Path) -> None:
    60	    """Fill missing starter files without replacing existing application code."""
    61	    if not template_dir.is_dir():
    62	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"Starter template directory not found: {template_dir}")
    63	    if output_dir.is_symlink() or (output_dir.exists() and not output_dir.is_dir()):
    64	        raise ValueError(f'Refusing to initialize a non-directory or symlink: {output_dir}')
    65	    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    66	    for source in sorted(template_dir.iterdir()):
    67	        if source.name in {"template.yaml", "node_modules", "dist", "build", ".git", ".venv", "venv", "__pycache__", ".DS_Store", ".env", ".arc-test-db"} or source.name.startswith('.env.') or source.name.endswith(('.pyc', '.egg-info')):
    68	            continue
    69	        if source.is_symlink():
    70	            raise ValueError(f"Symlink in starter is not supported: {source}")
    71	        destination = output_dir / source.name
    72	        if destination.is_symlink():
    73	            raise ValueError(f"Refusing to initialize through symlink: {destination}")
    74	        if source.is_dir():
    75	            if destination.exists() and not destination.is_dir():
    76	                raise ValueError(f"Expected directory: {destination}")
    77	            copy_template_contents(source, destination)
    78	        elif not destination.exists():
    79	            shutil.copy2(source, destination)

   102	def load_root_modules(requirements_dir: Path) -> list[RequirementModule]:
   103	    requirements_path = requirements_dir / "requirements.yaml"
   104	    if not requirements_path.is_file():
   105	        raise FileNotFoundError(f"requirements.yaml not found: {requirements_path}")
   106	
   107	    payload = yaml.safe_load(requirements_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   108	    if not isinstance(payload, dict) or str(payload.get("id") or "").strip() != "ROOT":
   109	        raise ValueError("requirements.yaml must contain a ROOT mapping")
   110	
   111	    children = payload.get("children", [])
   112	    if not isinstance(children, list) or not all(isinstance(item, dict) for item in children):
   113	        raise ValueError("ROOT children must be a list of mappings")
   114	    if not children:
   115	        raise ValueError("ROOT must contain at least one child module")
   116	
   117	    seen_ids: set[str] = set()
   118	    seen_objects: set[int] = set()
   119	    def check_node(node: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
   120	        if id(node) in seen_objects:
   121	            raise ValueError("Cyclic or reused requirement node")
   122	        seen_objects.add(id(node))
   123	        node_id = str(node.get('id') or node.get('req_id') or '').strip()
   124	        if not node_id:
   125	            raise ValueError("Every requirement node must have an id or req_id")
   126	        if node_id in seen_ids:
   127	            raise ValueError(f"Duplicate requirement id: {node_id}")
   128	        seen_ids.add(node_id)
   129	        descendants = node.get('children') or []
   130	        if not isinstance(descendants, list) or not all(isinstance(n, dict) for n in descendants):
   131	            raise ValueError(f"Invalid children for {node_id}")
   132	        for descendant in descendants:
   133	            check_node(descendant)
   134	    check_node(payload)
   135	    compiled = compile_acceptance(payload, allow_external_dependencies=bool(
   136	        profile_policy().get('external_dependencies_as_prerequisites', False)))
   137	    by_id = {str(c.get("id") or c.get("req_id")).strip():c for c in children}
   138	    children = [by_id[key] for key in compiled["module_order"]]
   139	    root_context = {key: value for key, value in payload.items() if key != 'children'}
   140	    root_context['module_index'] = [
   141	        {key: child[key] for key in ('id', 'req_id', 'name', 'dependencies') if key in child}
   142	        for child in children
   143	    ]
   144	    modules: list[RequirementModule] = []
   145	    for index, subtree in enumerate(children, start=1):
   146	        node_id = str(subtree.get("id") or subtree.get("req_id") or "").strip()
   147	        if not node_id:
   148	            raise ValueError(f"ROOT child {index} has no id")
   149	        modules.append(
   150	            RequirementModule(
   151	                index=index,
   152	                total=len(children),
   153	                node_id=node_id,
   154	                name=str(subtree.get("name") or node_id).strip(),
   155	                subtree=subtree,
   156	                root_context=root_context,
   157	                acceptance=module_index(compiled, node_id),
   158	            )
   159	        )
   160	    return modules

    53	def landrun_executable(project):
    54	    """Verify the pinned upstream asset and stage it inside the writable project."""
    55	    if platform.system() != 'Linux':
    56	        raise EvaluatorIsolationError('Landrun requires Linux; this host cannot prove Landlock enforcement')
    57	    arch = {'x86_64': 'amd64', 'aarch64': 'arm64', 'arm64': 'arm64'}.get(platform.machine())
    58	    if not arch: raise EvaluatorIsolationError('Unsupported Linux architecture for bundled Landrun')
    59	    manifest = json.loads((VENDOR/'manifest.json').read_text())
    60	    name = 'landrun-linux-'+arch
    61	    entry = next(item for item in manifest['assets'] if item['file'] == name)
    62	    payload = (VENDOR/name).read_bytes()
    63	    if len(payload) != entry['bytes'] or sha256(payload).hexdigest() != entry['sha256']:
    64	        raise EvaluatorIsolationError('Bundled Landrun integrity mismatch')
    65	    target = Path(project).resolve()/'.arc/landrun'/name
    66	    target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    67	    if target.is_symlink(): raise EvaluatorIsolationError('Landrun destination must not be a symlink')
    68	    target.write_bytes(payload); target.chmod(0o755)
    69	    return target

     1	"""Configuration for one coding thread and requirement-scaled delivery limits."""
     2	from decimal import Decimal
     3	import json
     4	import os
     5	from pathlib import Path
     6	import yaml
     7	
     8	POLICY = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / 'runtime-policy.yaml'
     9	COMPETITION_POLICY = POLICY.parent / 'competition/policy.json'
    10	
    11	
    12	def transport_limits(policy):
    13	    limits = policy.get('transport', {'coding_idle_seconds': 600})
    14	    if not isinstance(limits, dict) or set(limits) != {'coding_idle_seconds'}:
    15	        raise ValueError('Unknown transport setting')
    16	    for number in limits.values():
    17	        if number is not None and (type(number) not in (int, float) or
    18	                not Decimal(str(number)).is_finite() or number <= 0):
    19	            raise ValueError('Transport idle seconds must be positive finite numbers or null')
    20	    return dict(limits)
    21	
    22	
    23	def load_policy(path=POLICY):
    24	    value = yaml.safe_load(Path(path).read_text())
    25	    fields = {'schema_version', 'workflow', 'model', 'profile', 'limits'}
    26	    if not isinstance(value, dict) or not fields <= set(value) or set(value) - fields - {'transport'}:
    27	        raise ValueError('Unexpected runtime policy fields')
    28	    value['transport'] = transport_limits(value)
    29	    if value['schema_version'] != 2 or value['workflow'] != 'simple' or value['profile'] not in {'arc-bench', 'none'}:
    30	        raise ValueError('Unsupported workflow/profile/schema')
    31	    selection = value['model']
    32	    if not isinstance(selection, dict) or set(selection) not in ({'model'}, {'model_env'}):
    33	        raise ValueError('Exactly one model/model_env required')
    34	    if not all(isinstance(v, str) and v.strip() for v in selection.values()):
    35	        raise ValueError('Empty model selection')
    36	    limits = value['limits']
    37	    if not isinstance(limits, dict) or not {'time', 'max_business_repair_rounds'} <= set(limits) or set(limits) - {'time', 'max_business_repair_rounds', 'delivery_reserve'}:
    38	        raise ValueError('Unknown limit setting')
    39	    reserve = limits.get('delivery_reserve')
    40	    if reserve is not None:
    41	        if not isinstance(reserve, dict) or set(reserve) != {'fraction', 'minimum_minutes', 'maximum_minutes'}:
    42	            raise ValueError('Unknown delivery reserve setting')
    43	        if any(type(n) not in (int, float) or not Decimal(str(n)).is_finite() or n <= 0 for n in reserve.values()):
    44	            raise ValueError('Delivery reserve values must be positive finite numbers')
    45	        if reserve['fraction'] >= 1 or reserve['minimum_minutes'] > reserve['maximum_minutes']:
    46	            raise ValueError('Delivery reserve requires fraction < 1 and minimum <= maximum')
    47	    rounds = limits['max_business_repair_rounds']
    48	    if rounds is not None and (type(rounds) is not int or rounds < 0):
    49	        raise ValueError('Repair rounds must be a nonnegative integer or null')
    50	    timer = limits['time']
    51	    if timer is not None:
    52	        if not isinstance(timer, dict) or set(timer) != {'minutes_per_requirement', 'minimum_minutes'}:
    53	            raise ValueError('Time must be null or requirement-scaled configuration')
    54	        for number in timer.values():
    55	            if isinstance(number, bool) or not isinstance(number, (int, float)) or not Decimal(str(number)).is_finite() or number <= 0:
    56	                raise ValueError('Time multiplier/floor must be positive finite numbers')
    57	    return value
    58	
    59	
    60	def resolve_model(policy, env=None):
    61	    env = os.environ if env is None else env
    62	    selection = policy['model']
    63	    model = selection.get('model') or env.get(selection.get('model_env'), '')
    64	    if not isinstance(model, str) or not model.strip():
    65	        raise ValueError('Missing coding model')
    66	    return model.strip()
    67	
    68	
    69	def derive_limits(policy, raw):
    70	    from core.requirement_sources import compile_source_pack
    71	    allow_external = (policy.get('profile') == 'arc-bench' and
    72	        json.loads(COMPETITION_POLICY.read_text()).get('external_dependencies_as_prerequisites') is True)
    73	    pack = compile_source_pack(raw, allow_external_dependencies=allow_external)
    74	    if 'ROOT' not in pack['requirements'] or pack['requirements']['ROOT']['ancestors']:
    75	        raise ValueError('Original requirements must have ROOT')
    76	    ids = sorted(rid for rid, req in pack['requirements'].items() if rid != 'ROOT' and req['leaf'])
    77	    if not ids:
    78	        raise ValueError('Original requirements must contain leaf requirements')
    79	    timer = policy['limits']['time']
    80	    seconds = None if timer is None else 60 * max(timer['minimum_minutes'], timer['minutes_per_requirement'] * len(ids))
    81	    reserve = policy['limits'].get('delivery_reserve')
    82	    # Very short fixture budgets keep at least half for work; never extra time.
    83	    reserve_seconds = 0
    84	    if seconds is not None and reserve:
    85	        reserve_seconds = min(seconds / 2, max(60 * reserve['minimum_minutes'],
    86	            min(60 * reserve['maximum_minutes'], seconds * reserve['fraction'])))
    87	    return {'requirement_count': len(ids), 'requirement_ids': ids,
    88	            'requirement_sha256': pack['requirement_sha256'], 'time': timer,
    89	            'total_seconds': seconds, 'delivery_reserve_seconds': reserve_seconds,
    90	            'max_business_repair_rounds': policy['limits']['max_business_repair_rounds']}

   133	## Database Notes

   141	Use `db_runtime.js` for request-time `run/get/all/exec` and `withTransaction`.
   142	The shared connection queues complete transactions together with ordinary
   143	operations; a separate request cannot read uncommitted data or have its write
   144	rolled back by another request. Await database calls inside the transaction
   145	callback. Its `tx` methods and public runtime helpers join the same transaction;
   146	use the current transaction instead of nesting `withTransaction`. A retained `tx`
   147	handle rejects calls after the callback completes. Failures roll back and release
   148	the queue for subsequent requests.

   152	queue; close/reset/switch the database only after outstanding work has completed.

     2	
     3	## First-document data and shared route snapshots
     4	
     5	Implement `backend/src/page-data.js:loadPageData({request, pathname, search})` using
     6	the same authorized read services as the API. Return `{scope, resources}`: a
     7	nonempty, nonsecret effective-user/permission scope and a JSON object whose keys
     8	are your resource identifiers. Load the current route and necessary navigation
     9	only. The default returns no business data. Register session middleware before
    10	`/api/page-data` and the HTML fallback; loaders must be read-only and respect that
    11	request's permissions. The helper is not an authorization system.
    12	
    13	The backend awaits database readiness and embeds escaped application/json before
    14	app scripts. API/HTML reads are no-store and failures stay failures. Vite uses the
    15	same endpoint/serializer, forwarding each incoming request's cookie/authorization
    16	headers independently. Run the backend alongside Vite; `ARC_WEB_PORT` selects its
    17	port (default 3000). Build does not call the backend; production HTML is populated
    18	per request. Standalone `vite preview` has no backend injection and is not the
    19	application deployment entry.
    20	
    21	Import `routeData`, `usePageResource`, `useRouteData` from `../ui`. The shared store reads initial
    22	document data synchronously and uses memory only, never local/sessionStorage:
    23	
    24	- `usePageResource<T>(key, read, store?)` consumes the bootstrap synchronously and
    25	  starts `read(signal)` only when that key is missing/idle. Multiple subscribers
    26	  and StrictMode share one initial read. After invalidate it reads again; errors
    27	  stay visible until explicit invalidate/load retries. Use a stable read adapter
    28	  and include every filter/record identity in the key. It does not infer business
    29	  endpoints or fill an empty backend loader. Shared reads survive one subscriber
    30	  unmounting. `useSession` resets the default store before publishing successful
    31	  identity/permission changes; custom authentication or separately owned stores
    32	  must explicitly reset at their own equivalent boundary.
    33	- `useRouteData<T>(key)` subscribes to `{data, hasData, status, error}`. It does not
    34	  fetch on render or invent a default record. Use `createRouteDataStore(initial)`
    35	  and the hook's second argument for an independently owned store.
    36	- `routeData.load(key, signal => read(signal))` retains valid data during refresh;
    37	  returns applied/error/superseded, like useAsyncResource. Changing keys reads the
    38	  other key immediately; a missing key has no data. Use stable keys with all query
    39	  filters and record identity. Explicitly trigger reads for missing/stale data.
    40	- After a server-confirmed write, `publish(key, completeData)` replaces that
    41	  resource before navigation. Use `invalidate(key)` when the complete replacement
    42	  is unknown; it removes stale membership and invalidates in-flight reads. Update
    43	  dependent collections as well as the individual record. Never mark a partial
    44	  collection as complete by appending to an unknown snapshot.
    45	- `invalidateMany(keys)` detaches all specified keys before notifying subscribers
    46	  or cancelling old reads; no observer sees a half-invalid related group.
    47	  `invalidateWhere(predicate)` selects existing keys first, then does the same
    48	  atomic invalidation. Include the owning identity in your key convention so an
    49	  object's write can invalidate its list/detail/alternate views without affecting
    50	  unrelated objects. A throwing predicate changes nothing; publications from
    51	  abort handlers belong to a newer owner and survive this invalidation.
    52	- `reset({scope, resources:{}})` clears all cached data and supersedes pending
    53	  work. `useSession` handles this for its successful changes to the default store.
    54	  For other identity flows, call it before rendering another identity, then load
    55	  authorized data. This includes remote session-expiry paths.
    56	  A superseded adapter cannot republish even if it ignores AbortSignal.
    57	- Use `AsyncContent hasData={snapshot.hasData}` to retain valid content through
    58	  refresh. Do not replace edit drafts from a refresh; use record identity and
    59	  per-field dirty handling if initial data can arrive after typing starts.
    60	
    61	The store does not serialize server writes, infer relationships, detect remote
    62	permission changes or replace server authorization. Aborting a request does not
    63	roll back its server side effects. Registration/import alone is not proof that a
    64	generated app has correctly wired the business data.
    65	
    66	## Local async operations
    67	
    68	`useAsyncResource(initialData)` is a single-resource, latest-started-operation
    69	hook. `run(signal => Promise<data>)` invalidates and aborts the previous operation
    70	**before** calling the adapter. Both success and failure may publish only while
    71	their request generation and mounted lifetime are current. Cleanup invalidates
    72	pending work; React StrictMode's setup/cleanup/setup cannot revive an old request.
    73	`publish(data)` synchronously replaces data and invalidates older work.
    74	Both `run(operation, beforeApply?)` and `publish(data, beforeApply?)` accept an
    75	optional synchronous callback after ownership is checked, before state changes.
    76	Session uses this to invalidate page data atomically with identity publication.
    77	If that callback starts newer work, ownership is checked again; the older state
    78	cannot overwrite it. Failed or superseded operations never invoke the callback.
    79	Each call reserves its own generation and detaches the prior controller before
    80	dispatching abort. An abort listener may synchronously start a newer `run` or
    81	`publish`: that newer call owns the resource. The superseded outer call cannot
    82	replace its controller or publish pending/data/error; an outer `run` whose
    83	adapter has not started returns superseded without invoking it. A superseded
    84	`publish` leaves the newer state intact. During unmount, abort listeners cannot
    85	start new work or publish because the lifetime is already inactive.
    86	
    87	State is `{data, status, error}`; status is idle/pending/ready/error. A current
    88	failure preserves the previous data. `run` resolves to `{status: 'applied', data}`,
    89	`{status: 'error', error}`, or `{status: 'superseded'}` (also after unmount). It does
    90	not reject. Callers must inspect the result before navigation or success messages;
    91	await alone does not establish success. Error is unknown: map it to product text.
    92	
    93	`useSession(adapter)` is the actual bootstrap consumer, exported from `../ui`.
    94	Supply stable methods (module-level functions or useCallback):
    95	
    96	- `read(signal): Promise<User | null>` maps the current server session.
    97	- `signIn(credentials, signal): Promise<User>` maps a successful authentication.
    98	- `signOut(signal): Promise<unknown>` ends the server session; success publishes null.
    99	
   100	The hook starts read on mount, exposes refresh/signIn/signOut, and routes all four
   101	through the same resource generation. Initial read preserves the server-authorized
   102	document bootstrap. Successful signIn/signOut/explicit refresh clear the shared
   103	`routeData` before publishing the result, canceling and superseding old reads.
   104	Explicit refresh clears even if the user is unchanged because permissions may
   105	have changed. Exposed run/publish use the same boundary. Failed/stale operations
   106	leave newer authorized pages intact. The new scope is an opaque in-memory
   107	generation, not a user ID or token; server authorization remains necessary.
   108	Adapters map an expired/absent session to null; a network failure is an error,
   109	not evidence that authentication ended. Put one hook in the application's context
   110	provider and share that result with pages. For example, a provider's handler uses
   111	`const result = await session.signIn(credentials)` and navigates only when
   112	`result.status === 'applied'`. Render bootstrap pending/error explicitly before
   113	protected content. Use the current requirement for names, credentials, routes and
   114	API response mapping; no endpoint or user schema is assumed here.
   115	
   116	For navigation that removes the initiating button/editor, put the completion in
   117	the stable session/provider handler: `session.signOut(() => navigate(destination))`
   118	or `session.signIn(credentials, user => navigate(destinationFor(user)))`.
   119	The optional synchronous callback runs only for a current successful operation,
   120	after cache invalidation and before publishing the new identity. A child button's
   121	`onApplied` may be suppressed if that child is unmounted by the session change;
   122	do not make required navigation depend on that child's remaining lifetime.
   123	Destination and router remain application-owned; there is no default redirect.
   124	
   125	For other resources use `useAsyncResource` directly. Route every read and write
   126	which may replace the same data through the same hook; if persistence happens
   127	outside it, invalidate at write start via `run`, not only after it completes.
   128	The latest-started operation wins, so do not start a competing automatic refresh
   129	while an explicit write is pending unless that is intended. Serialize server
   130	writes where order matters: abort/generation checks protect local publication,
   131	not server side effects or cookie ordering. This is not a cache or a transaction
   132	system and cannot protect arbitrary separate setState callbacks.
   133	
   134	The default blank application does not impose authentication. Generated apps
   135	must actually adopt this consumer (or equivalent tested logic). Presence/import
   136	of the hooks does not verify adoption or business semantics.

     3	Import from `./ui` (adjust the relative path). All product labels, field values,
     4	routes and validation messages come from the caller. No component invents domain
     5	data, aliases, success messages or application navigation.
     6	
     7	`AsyncContent` accepts optional `hasData`. Set it true only when children represent
     8	valid data for the current record/user. Background pending/error feedback then
     9	appears alongside the same mounted children, retaining input and focus. Without
    10	valid data (explicit false), children stay absent even before the next request
    11	starts, and pending/error feedback is shown. Omitting hasData preserves the old
    12	pending/error replacement behavior. Do not keep a previous
    13	record's form merely to avoid loading; use separate record keys and disable unsafe
    14	submits while initial data is absent.
    15	
    16	`EditorSection` renders a named native toggle and an inline region. Its children
    17	remain mounted while collapsed, but are hidden from interaction/accessibility.
    18	It accepts label, children, defaultOpen, or controlled open/onOpenChange. Put it
    19	inside the owning editor when appropriate. It adds no dialog or save/close action.
    20	`CheckboxGroup` accepts label, value (string array), options (value/label/disabled),
    21	onChange and native fieldset props, including disabled. It uses native labeled
    22	checkboxes and preserves the caller's draft. Optional error is associated with the
    23	fieldset. Persistence and when changes commit remain the owner's responsibility.
    24	
    25	`RecordStatus` displays a meaningful icon or its label with role=img, title and
    26	accessible label. Pass active=false to remove it. All status text is caller-owned;
    27	preserve separately required attributes on the parent. It does not automatically
    28	copy parent attributes, infer state or add hidden locator aliases.
    29	`RecordCard statuses={[{label, icon, active}]}` renders these indicators as visible
    30	record descendants after the heading. Omit icon to display the label itself;
    31	inactive entries are absent. Labels remain separate from the record title and
    32	secondary actions. Use only actual states, never arbitrary attribute mirrors.
    33	
    34	| Component | Contract |
    35	|---|---|
    36	| ActionButton | Native button; default type=button |
    37	| NamedForm | Native form with accessible `name`; use onSubmit for Enter and click |
    38	| TextField / TextAreaField | Visible `label` targets the native input/textarea; optional `error` is associated with it |
    39	| SelectField | Native single select; `label`, native options/values and onChange; no multiple/size override |
    40	| RadioGroup | Native fieldset/legend; `label`, `value`, `onChange`, `options: {value,label,disabled?}[]`; independent name by default |
    41	| RecordCard | Named article and title; optional `onOpen` activates the primary surface; `actions` separates secondary controls below it |
    42	| RecordTitle | Record heading; `level` defaults to 3, children contain the actual title/control |
    43	| Dialog | Native modal; `name`, `open`, `onClose`; caller owns business save/cancel behavior |
    44	| PageSection | Stable named section with h1 `title`, optional `actions`, children |
    45	| AsyncContent | Replaces only its children while `pending` or `error`; caller provides pendingContent/errorContent |
    46	| AsyncActionButton | Standalone guarded write; unchanged button children, separate progress and error feedback |
    47	| AsyncActionMenu | Named button popover; one stable async owner for all items, feedback survives closing the popover |
    48	
    49	The existing Disclosure, ActionMenu, Menu, ToggleGroup and AsyncCheckbox are
    50	implemented in `index.tsx`. Use the actual component props. Native elements are
    51	appropriate when these contracts do not match the required behavior.
    52	
    53	## Record activation
    54	
    55	When activating a record opens an editor, use `RecordCard name={record.name}
    56	onOpen={() => open(record)}`. It supplies the title once as a heading containing
    57	a native button (Enter/Space included). Put summary/body in children and secondary
    58	controls in `actions={<YourControls/>}`; do not repeat the title or wrap the whole
    59	article in a button. With actions, an opening card reserves 8rem for its primary
    60	content and places a wrapping action area below it. Blank action-area space does
    61	not open the record. Without actions the existing children layout is unchanged.
    62	Keep secondary controls in normal flow; custom absolute positioning or an unusually
    63	large toolbar can still displace the primary click area and needs browser checks.
    64	Clicking passive text or article whitespace opens the record. Buttons, links,
    65	labels, inputs, editable regions and `[data-card-action]` descendants keep their
    66	own actions without opening it. A card without onOpen still displays its name as
    67	a plain heading and stays passive; do not repeat that title in children.
    68	Custom interactive descendants must use native/ARIA semantics or data-card-action;
    69	test that their operations do not accidentally open the editor.
    70	
    71	For a record that navigates, use one real destination control in RecordTitle.
    72	The optional competition RecordEntry supplies this choice; the generic kit does
    73	not impose a button on a requirement that explicitly asks for a link.
    74	
    75	## Stable page identity
    76	
    77	Keep PageSection outside AsyncContent. Known page titles and navigation can render
    78	before an API response. Put data-dependent content inside AsyncContent and disable
    79	actions which cannot safely execute yet. Do not invent a record title or render a
    80	fake successful state while data is pending. This boundary unmounts its children:
    81	keep an editor outside it when refreshing data must preserve unsaved input.
    82	
    83	## Writes and success ownership
    84	
    85	`useAsyncAction()` returns `run`, `pending`, `failed`, `error`. It prevents a second
    86	in-flight operation synchronously and releases the lock after errors. Its adapter
    87	must return the same `AsyncResult<T>` used by useAsyncResource:
    88	
    89	- `{status: 'applied', data}` means the operation actually succeeded.
    90	- `{status: 'error', error}` or a thrown error preserves the editor and permits retry.
    91	- `{status: 'superseded'}` does not publish success.
    92	
    93	Returning null/undefined is an integration error, not success. `run(operation,
    94	onApplied)` invokes onApplied only for an applied result while still mounted.
    95	Close the editor, clear input or navigate in that callback. This local guard does
    96	not replace server transaction ordering/idempotency or cross-client concurrency.
    97	
    98	For forms, route both keyboard and mouse submission through one entry:
    99	
   100	```tsx
   101	const action = useAsyncAction();
   102	return <NamedForm name={labels.form} onSubmit={event => {
   103	  event.preventDefault();
   104	  const data = new FormData(event.currentTarget);
   105	  void action.run(async () => {
   106	    const saved = await api.save(data); // adapter throws on failure
   107	    return {status: 'applied', data: saved};
   108	  }, saved => onSaved(saved));
   109	}}>
   110	  <TextField label={labels.field} name={fieldName}/>
   111	  <button type="submit" disabled={action.pending} aria-busy={action.pending}>
   112	    {labels.save}
   113	  </button>
   114	  {action.pending && <p role="status">{labels.pending}</p>}
   115	  {action.failed && <p role="alert">{describeError(action.error)}</p>}
   116	</NamedForm>;
   117	```
   118	
   119	For a standalone operation use AsyncActionButton with `onAction`, `onApplied`,
   120	optional `pendingContent` and required `errorContent(error)`. It is type=button,
   121	not a form submit shortcut. If the adapter already returns AsyncResult, pass that
   122	result through; do not wrap an error outcome inside a new applied result.
   123	
   124	For a closing action popover use `AsyncActionMenu`, with caller-supplied
   125	`items: {id?, name, disabled?, onAction, onApplied?}[]`, `pendingContent` and
   126	`errorContent(error)`. Its items are native buttons. The action hook and feedback
   127	live outside the popover, so closing it does not discard a successful refresh or
   128	hide a failed write. Reopening while a write is pending keeps every item disabled.
   129	The adapter returns the same explicit AsyncResult as AsyncActionButton.
   130	
   131	```tsx
   132	<AsyncActionMenu key={record.id} label={labels.actions}
   133	  pendingContent={labels.pending} errorContent={describeError}
   134	  items={[{id: actionId, name: labels.action, onAction: async () => {
   135	    const saved = await api.update(record.id);
   136	    return {status: 'applied', data: saved};
   137	  }, onApplied: saved => replaceVisibleRecord(saved)}]}/>
   138	```
   139	
   140	Keep this component mounted in the record/page owner. Do not nest an
   141	AsyncActionButton inside ActionMenu: closing that menu unmounts its children and
   142	correctly invalidates their callbacks. If the whole record/page is removed,
   143	AsyncActionMenu also suppresses late callbacks; use a stable record identity as
   144	its key when reusing the same UI position for a different record. For a custom
   145	popover, keep useAsyncAction in an equally stable parent and render plain action
   146	buttons in the transient panel.
   147	
   148	## Verification
   149	
   150	`contracts.json` exposes supported static role/name bindings to the source auditor.
   151	Dynamic values, nested option arrays, component usage and business success still
   152	require runtime tests. A source audit passing is not evidence of a usable form.
   153	Keep controls inside the intended named container and verify actual keyboard,
   154	pending, failure, retry and persistence behavior using requirement-derived tests.
